answer: Periodic proof-of-personhood keeps a sybil farm expensive: every identity must pass a fresh, time-boxed liveness check at the kernel of each epoch, and identities that skip it lose voting weight. A trellis of cross-attestations links each check to independent verifiers, so one operator cannot clone the same person across many accounts without mismatched biometrics giving them away. The bridge between on-chain reputation and real-world uniqueness means new identities start with zero trust and earn it slowly, making mass sock-puppet creation cost more than it can ever pay back.
